page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a baseline clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, large-block read-only memory bandwidth, and PassMark database operations, all scoring in the top 25 percent. Extended CPU instruction tests also rank in the top tier, aided by hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI. Conversely, the instance shows average performance in standard single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, software compilation, and Redis SET operations. Large-model LLM text generation represents a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25 percent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.16xlarge offers high compute density for workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration, avoiding the premium associated with those specialized hardware components. The instance is well-suited for compute-heavy tasks such as multi-threaded data decompression, database operations, and high-throughput web serving. It is less optimal for real-time large language model text generation or workloads requiring high-capacity local scratch space.
